post.caption: Six million sesterces, one pearl. The Roman writer Suetonius says Julius Caesar loved Servilia above all others. Servilia was the mother of Marcus Brutus, and in his first consulship, 59 BC, Caesar bought her a pearl. It cost six million sesterces. Caesar doubled a legionary's pay to about 900 sesterces a year, so the pearl cost more than 6,000 years of a soldier's pay. Suetonius wrote it down well over a century later, and nobody knows where the pearl came from. Historians call it Servilia's pearl. Caesar also limited pearls to people of a set rank and age.
